entry_state: Warranty service recognition follows the admitted performance measure. Contract modifications distinguish remaining distinct units from cumulative catch-up on an integrated promise. Principal/agent cases can share cash and profit but differ in revenue. Inventory and PPE preserve cost and consumption histories;sample-sale margin cannot reduce machine cost,and availability starts the admitted depreciation. The component-replacement example removes old carrying value and reconciles later disposal;its remaining method discussion continues next.
exit_state: Replacement retains dated source applicability. Revaluation allocates profit and OCI using each asset's own losses and surplus,while direct equity transfers create no income. Employee-benefit inputs remain measured assumptions. Impairment uses asset floors and redistributes constrained shares;recovery respects depreciated no-impairment ceilings and excludes goodwill reversal. All-zero carrying weights leave allocation unresolved. A separate provision needs its own obligation;the next case begins normal-capacity inventory overhead.

findings.observation: The two-asset revaluation case shows that equal total equity does not validate profit/OCI allocation. The zero adjustment for one asset still carries a new valuation record. Employee-benefit examples distinguish DBO,plan assets,net interest,remeasurement and employer cash.

The CGU example reallocates loss when A reaches its floor and preserves a residual when total capacity is insufficient. Reversal uses the no-impairment depreciation path. The zero-weight extension remains explicitly unresolved rather than receiving arbitrary weights.
